title: Replace a shared session with a session per request
problem: create_app opens one SQLAlchemy Session and every request uses it. After one duplicate username, every later request fails with PendingRollbackError, and a GET leaves its connection checked out. Refactor app.py so each request gets its own session from a yield dependency and the session is always closed.
requirements: Edit only app.py. Don't change conftest.py or test_users.py
create_app(engine) stores a sessionmaker for the engine (not a Session) on app.state
get_session(request) is a generator: it opens a session from that factory, yields it, and closes it even when the endpoint raises
A duplicate username still answers 409, and the next request works normally
Keep the endpoints, models and response shapes unchanged
contract: create_app(engine: Engine) -> FastAPI; get_session(request: Request) yields a Session
expectedBehavior: Two POSTs with the same username give 201 then 409; a third POST with a new name gives 201; after any request, no pool connection is still checked out
edgeCases: A request that fails with IntegrityError, followed by a normal request
A read-only request (GET) that never commits
An endpoint that raises HTTPException while the session is open
hints: Conceptual: a Session is a unit of work with its own transaction state, not a connection pool. Sharing one across requests means one request's failed flush poisons everyone else, and a read opens a transaction that nobody ends. The engine is the long-lived, shared object; sessions should be short-lived.

Specific: create the sessionmaker once in create_app and store it on app.state. get_session then becomes a dependency with yield: the code before yield runs before the endpoint, the code after it runs when the request is done.

Implementation: in create_app use app.state.session_factory = sessionmaker(engine). In get_session(request) write `with request.app.state.session_factory() as session:` and yield session inside the with block. Closing (the end of the with) rolls back anything uncommitted and returns the connection to the pool.
evaluation: No Session object outlives a request
The session is closed by a with block (or try/finally), not by a call at the end of each endpoint
You can explain why the duplicate broke every later request in the starter
